blocks.text: Lots and land in Central Coquitlam

items.t: Established-street house lots: freehold detached houses across the central streets under the City's small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 in Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996. Subdivision minimums as the City states them: 650 m² with 18.5 m width for R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width for R-2. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size — the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel. A fee-simple lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.
Serviced vs unserviced, as the City states it: Critically for lot value: lots not connected to municipal water or sewer are outside the City's SSMUH rules.
Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any ALR rule.

Watercourse-shaped land: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam; Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks from watercourses and s.523 covers riparian areas. Gross lot area is not buildable area on creek and ravine lots.

Hideaway Park (Coquitlam Hideaway Mobile Home Park) — 4200 Dewdney Trunk Road (Ranch Park). PAD-RENTAL PARK: The same marketing document notes the site falls within a "Shoulder Station Area" in the City's Transit-Oriented Development Strategy with potential to be rezoned to multifamily use — a redevelopment-risk fact a park buyer must weigh.
Pine & Glen — 1175 Pinetree Way (Onni): It sells strata condominiums, not lots; the 186 rental apartments are rental-only.
Applications and rezoning proposals, where they exist, are documented as proposals only — never as for-sale inventory.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Central Coquitlam

items.t: Municipality: City of Coquitlam, BC — Central Coquitlam is the established central part of the city, around Como Lake Avenue, Austin Avenue and the City Centre / Pinetree Way edge. "Central Coquitlam" is the GVR sub-area name as it appears in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.

Nearby areas: Coquitlam West / Southwest Coquitlam to the west, City Centre (North Coquitlam in the board naming) to the north-east, Burke Mountain beyond, Maillardville to the south, Port Moody to the west.

Main roads: Como Lake Avenue, Austin Avenue, Pinetree Way and Guildford Way. Transit: the Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line) stations Coquitlam Central, Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas serve the City Centre edge on Pinetree Way and Barnet Highway, and Coquitlam Central also has West Coast Express service.

Schools: SD43 catchments are address-based, in a three-tier district (elementary / middle / secondary). SD43 schools named for central Coquitlam on district pages include Central Elementary School, Hillcrest Middle School and École Dr. Charles Best Secondary School; catchments for other addresses must be checked in the locator.

Parks and services: Town Centre Park and Como Lake Park are City park names in City records for this part of Coquitlam; City Centre Aquatic Complex and Evergreen Cultural Centre are in the City Centre area at the sub-area's east edge. Coquitlam Public Library City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way, and Poirier branch, 575 Poirier Street, serve Coquitlam. Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, is the nearest hospital for this area.

Market context, labelled correctly (September 2026, SnapStats GVR September 2026 report): Central Coquitlam sub-area detached inventory 64 / sales 9 (14% ratio) and "Condos & Townhomes" combined 36 / 5 (14% ratio); Coquitlam community detached median $1,455,000 ($550/sqft, 97% sale-to-list, 35 days on market) and attached median $625,000 ($687/sqft, 96%, 23 days). SnapStats has no land category — none of these figures is a land figure.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Central Coquitlam

items.t: Bare-land strata block (no bare-land strata plan is documented in Central Coquitlam; stated for the form, which the zoning bylaw permits only with roadway access to each strata lot): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children). A listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules: ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; residence caps principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); farm class is three-tier ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31). No farm-class parcel in Central Coquitlam is confirmed, and a flat "$2,500+" figure is not accurate wherever it appears.

City of Coquitlam property tax payment was due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance of current taxes after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after September 15, 2026 (including unclaimed Home Owner Grants). Utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste; the City's 2026 budget materials record an average-household total property-charges increase of $137 combined.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Coquitlam

items.t: The OCP changed in April 2026: Coquitlam adopted its Interim Official Community Plan (Bylaws 5511/5512) on April 27, 2026, superseding OCP No. 3479, 2001 — the City states it streamlined the old plan and added no new land-use policy except as provincial legislation required, with a fuller OCP update project anticipated to begin in 2027. A seller's disclosure or an old summary citing Bylaw 3479 is a generation out of date.
Services decide density here, not just lot size: the SSMUH unit counts (3 / 4 units) expressly exclude lots not connected to municipal water or sewer.

The servicing bill has a name and a number: subdivision servicing in Coquitlam runs under Bylaw No. 3558, 2003 — a 2003 bylaw still being amended in July 2026 — including owner-paid City-installed signage and solicitor-approved statutory rights-of-way for services. A split priced without a Bylaw 3558 servicing estimate is priced blind.

The cheapest "land" in the sub-area is not land: Hideaway Park's pads rent — the park's own development-marketing document pairs its 68 pads / 5.76 acres with a Shoulder Station multifamily-rezoning note, so the tenure risk is documented in the seller-side material itself, not just in buyer caution.

items.t: Central Coquitlam is the established central part of Coquitlam, around Como Lake Avenue and Austin Avenue, reaching the City Centre / Pinetree Way edge.
The City plans this part of Coquitlam through City Centre and Town Centre planning and its Transit-Oriented Areas framework, not a Central Coquitlam plan.
Neighbours are Coquitlam West to the west, City Centre to the north-east, Burke Mountain beyond, Maillardville to the south and Port Moody to the west.
Main roads are Como Lake Avenue, Austin Avenue, Pinetree Way and Guildford Way.
The stock mixes freehold detached houses on the established central streets with strata apartments clustered near Pinetree Way and the City Centre stations.
Oasis, 2955 Atlantic Avenue, is a 42-storey, 255-unit concrete strata high-rise built in 2012 by Onni, strata plan BCS4512.
MThree, 1188 Pinetree Way, is a 48-storey, 319-unit concrete strata high-rise built in 2016 by Cressey, strata plan EPS2687.

items.t: The Central Coquitlam-specific rule is proximity: lots near the Pinetree Way stations sit inside the City's Transit-Oriented Areas framework, while Como Lake streets do not.

items.t: SD43 is a three-tier district — elementary, middle and secondary — unlike two-tier districts nearby.

Coquitlam Central is both a SkyTrain station and a West Coast Express station, so downtown commuter-rail trips start there.

blocks.text: Central Coquitlam: development and new projects

items.t: Southwest Shoulders and Corridors / Transit-Oriented Areas Update — Austin Avenue corridor, City of Coquitlam: Council adopted the amendments on May 27, 2026 after a public hearing, creating medium-density housing, townhousing and local commercial opportunities around the Burquitlam and Lougheed stations and along Austin Avenue, with a new neighbourhood commercial node near Austin Avenue and Blue Mountain Street and about 2,300 additional homes expected under the concepts; status: adopted (as of November 3, 2026).
The Central angle is only the due date that applies to every lot here: Coquitlam property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with 5% penalties after July 2 and after September 15, 2026.
Three Millennium Line stations — Coquitlam Central, Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas — serve the neighbourhood's City Centre edge.
Como Lake Avenue, Austin Avenue, Pinetree Way and Guildford Way are the main roads through Central Coquitlam.
West Coast Express service is available at Coquitlam Central Station.

blocks.text: Central Coquitlam: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check creek and ravine setbacks before pricing any addition or rebuild on a watercourse lot.
The Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area reaches 30 metres from the top of bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam.
Confirm the exact zone and municipal services before advertising suite, carriage-home or multi-unit potential, because unserviced lots fall outside the small-scale multi-unit housing rules.

faq.q: Is there a vacant-lot subdivision I can buy into in Central Coquitlam?
faq.a: Land trades as built house lots on the Como Lake / Austin streets, strata units at the City Centre edge, and (at Hideaway Park) a home on a rented pad.

faq.q: Can a house lot add units?
faq.a: Yes under the City's SSMUH rules — up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes — but lots not connected to municipal water or sewer fall outside the rules, so confirm services and the exact zone first.

faq.q: Why can't I find the City Centre towers under "Central Coquitlam"?
faq.a: Because listing feeds label the tower cluster North Coquitlam / Canyon Springs / Town Centre, not Central Coquitlam — a "Central Coquitlam" board filter misses them.

faq.q: Is Hideaway Park a way to own cheap land in Coquitlam?
faq.a: You never own the land, and the document itself flags potential multifamily rezoning in a Shoulder Station Area — price the redevelopment risk, not a land value.

No — Pine & Glen (1175 Pinetree Way, Onni) is a presale of 705 strata condominiums plus 186 market-rental apartments in three towers over a podium, estimated completion 2028. Presale LOT offerings in the sub-area: zero verified.

faq.q: Can I buy just one side of a duplex in Central Coquitlam?
faq.a: Only if that side is legally separate — a strata lot in a 2-lot strata plan, or its own fee-simple lot from a subdivision. Check the title first.

faq.q: Is Hideaway Park a duplex or half-duplex purchase?
faq.a: No. It is a manufactured-home park on rented pads — you own the home and rent the site at 4200 Dewdney Trunk Road.

faq.q: Is there a named duplex development in Central Coquitlam?
faq.a: The duplex evidence here is the form class under Coquitlam's small-scale residential zoning.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Central Coquitlam address?
faq.a: School District 43 (SD43) catchments are set by exact address in a three-tier system of elementary, middle and secondary schools. Charles Best Secondary. Run the exact address.

faq.q: Which SkyTrain stations can I use?
faq.a: Three Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line) stations serve the City Centre edge of Central Coquitlam: Coquitlam Central, Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas, on Pinetree Way and Barnet Highway. Coquitlam Central also offers West Coast Express commuter rail. Interior streets around Como Lake and Austin Avenue have no station inside the neighbourhood, so most trips start with a bus or drive to a station.

faq.q: What recreation is actually in the area?
faq.a: Town Centre Park and Como Lake Park are the City park names recorded for this part of Coquitlam, and the City Centre Aquatic Complex and Evergreen Cultural Centre sit at the City Centre edge. Como Lake Park is at 700 Gatensbury Street.
